OFFLINE REPORT LAB

Run from this folder with Node.js (verified with v26.13.0):

  node lab.cjs

To also execute the original isolated encoder on the captured synthetic reports:

  node lab.cjs --encode

No package installation is needed. Open the index.html path printed by the command.
Each run creates a new directory under runs, with report.json and captures/*.bin.
The HTML and JSON label pre-encoding inputs and encoded outputs separately.
To choose a new or empty output directory:

  node lab.cjs --out runs/my-inspection --json

Run verification:

  node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/*.test.cjs

WHAT EXECUTES

The native cases instantiate eight small isolated helper bodies copied from the
reviewed 60946132 module. Frame observations, the selected record descriptor,
context pointers and session data are controlled fixtures. The complete game
does not load or run. Original native envelope builders call a local recorder
at their encoder-input boundary. This boundary returns zero, so the downstream
sender never runs. Those captures are native input structures before encoding.

With --encode, two captured synthetic inputs are separately replayed through
the original isolated f22860 encoder, with its seven actual leaf helpers linked. The
encoder has no transport implementation. Its returned bytes are saved locally;
an independent checksum check and short-buffer cases inspect the result and
capacity handling. This executes selected serialization paths, not every
message schema, the full client or an actual online report exchange.

The page-check cases use pinned source in an isolated VM. They compare clean
APIs with the actual extension startup wrapper. A separate minimal-module case
demonstrates explicit local loading without replacing browser APIs. That case
does not establish compatibility of a full patched game.

NETWORK BOUNDARY

The CLI blocks common networking, subprocess and worker APIs in its own Node
process. Native fixtures have exact import allowlists; the page-check VM has
no network or process capability. The local HTML viewer has no scripts and a
Content Security Policy that blocks connections and external assets. No HTTP
server is needed. This is not an OS firewall or a general untrusted-code sandbox.

Fixtures and provenance are bundled and hash-pinned. No official-site requests,
accounts, browser sessions, external services or installed-extension changes
are part of a run. Historical reports and private server decisions are absent.
A clean controlled case does not prove multiplayer safety.

CONTINUING THE OFFLINE WORK

lib/local-loader.cjs is the shared entry point. It accepts local bytes and a
complete expected SHA-256, checks the source, applies explicitly supplied patch
steps, checks every step's expected input/output hash, then compiles directly.
It does not fetch files, intercept browser APIs, supply imports, instantiate a
game or start an entry point. Each caller must provide its own bounded imports
and decide whether to instantiate its verified isolated module.

To adapt an existing pure patcher, provide a transform record:

  {
    name: 'Reviewed offline patch',
    inputSha256: VERIFIED_INPUT_HASH,
    outputSha256: VERIFIED_OUTPUT_HASH,
    apply: bytes => existingPatcher(bytes)
  }

The current native fixtures already use the shared loader. Future work can add
one reviewed patch/controller integration at a time and compare its observations
with the clean baseline, while retaining the reporting checks and local capture.
This does not implement a complete playable offline client. Matching assets,
host/worker ABIs, rendering, audio, input and saves still require integration.

'use strict';

const crypto = require('node:crypto');

const hash = bytes => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');

function checkedHash(value, field) {
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(value)) {
    throw new TypeError(`${field} must be a complete lowercase SHA-256 hash.`);
  }
  return value;
}

function copyBytes(value, label) {
  if (value instanceof ArrayBuffer) return new Uint8Array(value.slice(0));
  if (value instanceof Uint8Array) return Uint8Array.from(value);
  throw new TypeError(`${label} must be a Uint8Array or ArrayBuffer.`);
}

// Explicit, local compilation. No fetch, browser interception, automatic imports,
// game entry point, network transport, or module instantiation is supplied here.
async function compilePinnedLocalModule({ bytes, expectedSha256, label = 'Local module', transforms = [] } = {}) {
  checkedHash(expectedSha256, 'expectedSha256');
  if (!Array.isArray(transforms)) throw new TypeError('transforms must be an array.');
  const apiBefore = {
    Module: WebAssembly.Module,
    Instance: WebAssembly.Instance,
    compile: WebAssembly.compile,
    compileStreaming: WebAssembly.compileStreaming,
    instantiate: WebAssembly.instantiate,
    instantiateStreaming: WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming,
    Memory: WebAssembly.Memory
  };
  const otherAPIs = [
    [globalThis, 'WebAssembly', globalThis.WebAssembly],
    [globalThis, 'Worker', globalThis.Worker],
    [globalThis, 'SharedArrayBuffer', globalThis.SharedArrayBuffer],
    [globalThis, 'MessagePort', globalThis.MessagePort],
    [Function.prototype, 'toString', Function.prototype.toString]
  ];
  for (const constructor of [globalThis.Worker, globalThis.MessagePort]) {
    if (constructor?.prototype) otherAPIs.push([constructor.prototype, 'postMessage', constructor.prototype.postMessage]);
  }
  function assertAPIIdentity(stage) {
    for (const [name, original] of Object.entries(apiBefore)) {
      if (WebAssembly[name] !== original) throw new Error(`${label}: WebAssembly API ${name} changed ${stage}.`);
    }
    for (const [owner, name, original] of otherAPIs) {
      if (owner[name] !== original) throw new Error(`${label}: API ${name} changed ${stage}.`);
    }
  }
  let current = copyBytes(bytes, label);
  const inputSha256 = hash(current);
  if (inputSha256 !== expectedSha256) throw new Error(`${label}: input hash mismatch.`);
  const applied = [];

  for (const step of transforms) {
    if (!step || typeof step.name !== 'string' || !step.name.trim() || typeof step.apply !== 'function') {
      throw new TypeError('Each transform requires a name and an explicit apply function.');
    }
    checkedHash(step.inputSha256, `${step.name}.inputSha256`);
    checkedHash(step.outputSha256, `${step.name}.outputSha256`);
    if (hash(current) !== step.inputSha256) throw new Error(`${step.name}: transform input hash mismatch.`);
    current = copyBytes(await step.apply(Uint8Array.from(current)), step.name);
    const output = hash(current);
    if (output !== step.outputSha256) throw new Error(`${step.name}: transform output hash mismatch.`);
    assertAPIIdentity(`during transform ${step.name}`);
    applied.push({ name: step.name, inputSha256: step.inputSha256, outputSha256: output });
  }

  assertAPIIdentity('before compilation');
  const module = await WebAssembly.compile(current);
  assertAPIIdentity('during compilation');
  return {
    module,
    inputSha256,
    moduleSha256: hash(current),
    byteLength: current.byteLength,
    transforms: applied,
    globalAPIsChanged: false
  };
}

module.exports = { compilePinnedLocalModule };

# Synthetic NOS top-up source update

Working extension version0.42.8 now provides a session-only **Keep NOS topped up** switch alongside **Award once**. Both use the same verified native synthetic STYLE_NEARMISS bridge; the direct `Engine.refill` API remains disabled. The loop has no speed threshold.

Top-up starts off and is not restored by saved NOS/profile selections. It samples effective NOS before each request, waits at full or overfull and resumes when consumption drops below full. Active accounting credit is adjusted by the original clock domain's elapsed ticks; raw stored LEFT alone is not treated as the current level. Two read-only samples must agree on capacity, credit, activation timestamp and clock domain, with current owned car/race identity.

The loop shares the manual controller's single outstanding slot. It waits at least250ms after observing a matching positive native NOS completion before another request. Focus/permission loss pauses and requests cancellation; F7/F9, car/session replacement, game exit, uncertain outcomes or confirmed style without positive observed NOS disarm it. A late receipt may settle an old request but never silently re-arms the loop.

function freezeExtension(relative) {
  const directory = path.join(ROOT, relative);
  const manifestBytes = fs.readFileSync(path.join(directory, 'manifest.json'));
  const manifest = JSON.parse(manifestBytes);
  const sources = new Map(manifest.content_scripts[0].js.map(name => [name, fs.readFileSync(path.join(directory, name), 'utf8')]));
  return {directory, manifest, manifestHash: sha(manifestBytes), sources,
    fileHashes: Object.fromEntries([...sources].map(([name, source]) => [name, sha(source)]))};
}

function browserStandIns() {
  const sent = [], workers = [];
  // Function#toString is never replaced. Native bound functions/proxies are
  // explicitly synthetic browser stand-ins, not claims about browser identity.
  const nativePost = new Proxy(Array.prototype.push.bind([]), {apply(_target, receiver, args) {
    const entry = {message: args[0], rest: args.slice(1)};
    receiver.sent.push(entry);sent.push(entry);return undefined;
  }});
  const nativeTerminate = new Proxy(Array.prototype.pop.bind([]), {apply(_target, receiver) {receiver.terminated = true;}});
  const prototype = {
    postMessage: nativePost, terminate: nativeTerminate,
    addEventListener(type, callback) {(this.handlers[type] ??= []).push(callback);},
    removeEventListener(type, callback) {this.handlers[type] = (this.handlers[type] || []).filter(fn => fn !== callback);},
    emit(data) {const event = {data, stopped: false, stopImmediatePropagation(){this.stopped = true;}};
      for (const callback of this.handlers.message || []) {callback(event);if (event.stopped) break;}}
  };
  const Worker = new Proxy(Array.bind(null), {
    get(target, key, receiver) {return key === 'prototype' ? prototype : Reflect.get(target, key, receiver);},
    construct(_target, args) {
      const worker = Object.assign(Object.create(prototype), {url: String(args[0]), handlers: {}, sent: []});
      workers.push(worker);return worker;
    }
  });
  const portPrototype = {postMessage: new Proxy(Array.prototype.push.bind([]), {apply(){}})};
  const MessagePort = new Proxy(Array.bind(null), {get(target, key, receiver) {
    return key === 'prototype' ? portPrototype : Reflect.get(target, key, receiver);
  }});
  return {Worker, MessagePort, sent, workers, prototype};
}
function storage(map) {
  return {getItem: key => map.get(String(key)) ?? null,
    setItem: (key, value) => map.set(String(key), String(value)), removeItem: key => map.delete(String(key))};
}
const hostAPIs = Object.fromEntries(['Memory', 'Module', 'Instance', 'instantiate', 'instantiateStreaming', 'compile', 'compileStreaming']
  .map(key => [key, WebAssembly[key]]));
const flush = () => new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve));
function observation(state, context, worker) {
  const predicate = state.guard.predicate;
  const selected = {
    'WebAssembly.Memory': context.WebAssembly.Memory,
    'WebAssembly.Module': context.WebAssembly.Module, 'WebAssembly.Instance': context.WebAssembly.Instance,
    'WebAssembly.instantiate': context.WebAssembly.instantiate,
    'WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming': context.WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming,
    'WebAssembly.compileStreaming': context.WebAssembly.compileStreaming,
    Worker: context.Worker, 'Worker.prototype.postMessage': context.Worker?.prototype?.postMessage,
    SharedArrayBuffer: context.SharedArrayBuffer,
    'MessagePort.prototype.postMessage': context.MessagePort?.prototype?.postMessage
  };
  const marks = state.guard.read();
  return {
    marks, categories: Object.entries(state.guard.categories).filter(([, bit]) => marks & bit).map(([name]) => name),
    selectedAPI: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(selected).map(([name, value]) => [name, {
      exists: typeof value !== 'undefined', type: typeof value, predicatePasses: predicate(value)
    }])),
    memoryPrototypeIsHostFunctionPrototype: Object.getPrototypeOf(context.WebAssembly.Memory) === Function.prototype,
    compileStreamingIdentityUnchanged: context.WebAssembly.compileStreaming === hostAPIs.compileStreaming,
    compileIdentityUnchanged: context.WebAssembly.compile === hostAPIs.compile,
    workerConstructorIdentityUnchanged: context.Worker === state.browser.Worker,
    instancePostMessage: worker ? {predicatePasses: predicate(worker.postMessage),
      ownProperty: Object.hasOwn(worker, 'postMessage'), checkedByCapturedGuard: false} : null,
    helperFlags: state.guard.helperFlags(),
    knownGlobals: state.guard.knownGlobals.filter(name => context[name] !== undefined),
    knownSettings: settingsKeys.filter(key => context.localStorage.getItem(key) !== null),
    extensionGlobalNames: Object.getOwnPropertyNames(context).filter(name => /^__NFSU2_|^__nfsu2DrivingTools$/.test(name)).sort(),
    patchPhase: context.__NFSU2_AI__?.patchState?.phase ?? 'absent'
  };
}

async function runCase(label, extension, originalModule) {
  const state = {label, stages: [], browser: browserStandIns(), fetches: [], logs: []};
  let context;
  const capture = (name, worker) => state.stages.push({name, ...observation(state, context, worker)});
  const compatibility = {
    originalModule,
    bootstrap(seed, stores) {
      // Discard only pre-evaluation DOM-fixture placeholders. Actual extension
      // globals are subsequently created and observed without removal.
      context = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(seed).filter(([name]) => !name.startsWith('__NFSU2_')));
      context.window = context.top = context;
      context.WebAssembly = Object.create(Object.getPrototypeOf(WebAssembly), Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors(WebAssembly));
      context.Worker = state.browser.Worker;context.MessagePort = state.browser.MessagePort;
      context.SharedArrayBuffer = SharedArrayBuffer;
      context.crypto = crypto.webcrypto;context.TextEncoder = TextEncoder;context.TextDecoder = TextDecoder;
      context.atob = atob;context.AbortController = AbortController;context.structuredClone = structuredClone;
      context.localStorage = storage(stores.profileStorage);context.sessionStorage = storage(stores.sessions);
      context.fetch = async (url, options) => {
        state.fetches.push({url: String(url), cache: options?.cache, credentials: options?.credentials});
        if (url === '/game.json') return {ok: true, json: async () => ({...metadata})};
        if (String(url).startsWith('/game.wasm')) return {ok: true,
          arrayBuffer: async () => rawBytes.buffer.slice(rawBytes.byteOffset, rawBytes.byteOffset + rawBytes.byteLength)};
        throw Error('Fixture denied nonlocal resource ' + url);
      };
      context.console = {log(){},error(){},warn(value){state.logs.push(String(value));}};
      state.guard = makeGuard(context, {get: key => context.localStorage.getItem(key)}, settingsKeys, context.console);
      capture('clean-browser-baseline');
      assert.equal(state.stages.at(-1).marks, 0, 'Clean baseline must be free of realm/stand-in artifacts');
      for (const [name, source] of extension.sources) if (name !== 'page.js')
        vm.runInNewContext(source, context, {filename: path.join(extension.directory, name), timeout: 3000});
      capture('all-manifest-scripts-before-page');
      return context;
    },
    runPage(context) {
      vm.runInNewContext(extension.sources.get('page.js'), context, {filename: path.join(extension.directory, 'page.js'), timeout: 3000});
    },
    afterStartup(_context) {capture('actual-page-startup');},
    afterWorker(_context, worker) {capture('actual-game-worker-created', worker);},
    marks: () => state.guard.read(),
    async afterBoot(_context, worker, originalMessage) {
      for (let attempts = 0; attempts < 500 && worker.sent.length === 0; attempts++)
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));
      assert.equal(worker.sent.length, 1, 'Actual worker postMessage eventually forwards once: ' +
        JSON.stringify({fetches: state.fetches, patchState: context.__NFSU2_AI__?.patchState}));
      const forwarded = worker.sent[0].message;
      assert.deepEqual(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(forwarded.cfg)), JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(originalMessage.cfg)), 'Actual cfg.env including page report marker preserved');
      state.boot = {
        cfgBefore: originalMessage.cfg, cfgAfter: forwarded.cfg,
        originalModuleWasReplaced: forwarded.mod !== originalMessage.mod,
        compiledProfileRevision: context.__NFSU2_AI__?.getModuleProfile?.(forwarded.mod)?.revision ?? null,
        compiledProfileHash: context.__NFSU2_AI__?.getModuleProfile?.(forwarded.mod)?.hash ?? null,
        nativeSyntheticNearMiss: context.__NFSU2_AI__?.getModuleProfile?.(forwarded.mod)?.capabilities.nativeSyntheticNearMiss===true,
        patchState: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(context.__NFSU2_AI__?.patchState || {})),
        cfgPreserved: true, reportMarkerPreserved: forwarded.cfg.env.NFSU2_PAGE_MARKS === originalMessage.cfg.env.NFSU2_PAGE_MARKS
      };
      capture('actual-boot-forwarded', worker);
    }
  };
  const f = await fixtureContext.makeActualPageFixture(null, false, false, compatibility);
  f.run(4);
  capture('four-page-ticks', f.worker);
  state.localStorageKeys = [...f.profileStorage.keys()];state.sessionStorageKeys = [...f.sessions.keys()];
  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(hostAPIs).filter(key => WebAssembly[key] !== hostAPIs[key]), [], 'Host native APIs are unchanged');
  return {label, version: extension.manifest.version, manifestSha256: extension.manifestHash,
    stages: state.stages, boot: state.boot, fetches: state.fetches,
    storage: {local: state.localStorageKeys, session: state.sessionStorageKeys}, hostHelperWarnings: state.logs.length};
}

function calibrations() {
  const results = [];
  for (const name of ['known-global', 'known-setting', 'public-helper-getter', 'module-helper-getter', 'passive-helper-read']) {
    const browser = browserStandIns(), entries = new Map();
    const context = {WebAssembly, Worker: browser.Worker, MessagePort: browser.MessagePort,
      SharedArrayBuffer, localStorage: storage(entries)};
    const logs = [], guard = makeGuard(context, {get: key => context.localStorage.getItem(key)}, settingsKeys, {warn: value => logs.push(String(value))});
    assert.equal(guard.read(), 0);
    if (name === 'known-global') context.__nosCheat = true;
    if (name === 'known-setting') entries.set(settingsKeys[0], '{}');
    if (name === 'public-helper-getter') void context.__nfsu2.session;
    if (name === 'module-helper-getter') void context.Module;
    if (name === 'passive-helper-read') {void context.__nfsu2.phase;void context.__nfsu2.fps;context.__nfsu2.displayHz();}
    const expected = {'known-global': 4, 'known-setting': 8, 'public-helper-getter': 16, 'module-helper-getter': 32, 'passive-helper-read': 0}[name];
    assert.equal(guard.read(), expected);
    results.push({name, marks: guard.read(), helperFlags: guard.helperFlags(), warnings: logs.length,
      scope: 'Independent synthetic positive control using exact captured getter/predicate source; not extension behavior'});
  }
  return results;
}

async function main() {
  // Actual original module is compiled locally only, never instantiated.
  const originalModule = await WebAssembly.compile(rawBytes);
  const cases = [await runCase('updated-all-manifest-actual-page', updated, originalModule),
    await runCase('baseline0426-all-manifest-actual-page', baseline, originalModule)];
  const controls = calibrations();
  assert.equal(cases[0].boot.nativeSyntheticNearMiss,true,'Updated complete worker module must contain the verified synthetic award adapter');
  assert.equal(cases[1].boot.nativeSyntheticNearMiss,false,'Historical baseline retains its original capabilities');
  for (const extension of [updated, baseline]) {
    assert.equal(sha(fs.readFileSync(path.join(extension.directory, 'manifest.json'))), extension.manifestHash, 'Manifest changed during frozen check');
    for (const [name, expected] of Object.entries(extension.fileHashes))
      assert.equal(sha(fs.readFileSync(path.join(extension.directory, name))), expected, 'Source changed during frozen check: ' + name);
  }
  const receipt = {
    at: new Date().toISOString(), sourceFreeze: 'source-freeze.json', sourceFreezeSha256: sha(fs.readFileSync(path.join(OUT, 'source-freeze.json'))),
    runtime: process.version, fullGameInstantiated: false, realWorkerCreated: false, networkUsed: false,
    reportTransportAvailable: false, originalModuleCompileOnly: true, settingsKeys,
    harnessSourceSha256: sha(fs.readFileSync(__filename)),
    domFixtureSourceSha256: sha(fs.readFileSync(fixtureFile)), adaptedDOMFixtureSha256: sha(fixtureSource),
    exactCapturedSource: freeze.host, cases, controls,
    limitations: [
      'Controlled Node DOM/browser stand-ins are not an actual Chrome session or an account record.',
      'Worker and MessagePort constructors/prototype methods are explicitly native-callable proxy stand-ins. Function.prototype.toString and API toString methods are not overridden.',
      'The captured guard runs in the host Function realm so native Memory prototype comparison does not create a VM realm false positive.',
      'Known settings use the exact captured key list and default predicate; its B.get provider is a synthetic localStorage adapter.',
      'Actual captured helper getters set their own observational flags. No report markers are removed or rewritten.',
      'The current original WASM and actual transformed module are compiled and forwarded only. No game module instance or original sender exists.',
      'Tools remain at startup defaults. Four page ticks use synthetic16MiB fixture memory without an original game data image; this does not exercise active driving, user tool actions or JOIN.',
      'The synthetic memory would not satisfy the original full module memory import minimum if instantiated. The Worker stand-in only records forwarded arguments.',
      'Captured predicate observations do not establish server acceptance, an account sanction or multiplayer safety.'
    ]
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, 'updated-host-check-receipt.json'), JSON.stringify(receipt, null, 2) + '\n');
  console.log(JSON.stringify({version: updated.manifest.version, scripts: updated.sources.size,
    cases: cases.map(item => ({label: item.label, stages: item.stages.map(stage => ({name: stage.name, marks: stage.marks, categories: stage.categories})), boot: item.boot})), controls}, null, 2));
}

    ['race-pace-factor','race-pace-value','racePaceFactor',0.75,3,1,'1.00×'],
    ['corner-factor','corner-value','cornerFactor',0.6,0.95,0.8,'0.80×'],
    ['pace-factor','pace-value','paceFactor',0.75,3,1,'1.00×'],
    ['power','power-value','power',1,3,1.5,'1.5×'],

    ['rpm','rpm-value','rpm',3000,10000,6500,'6500']
  ]) {
    assert.match(f.html(),new RegExp('id="'+id+'"[^>]*type="range"'));

    f.input(id,20000);assert.equal(f.nodes[id].value,high);assert.equal(f.prefs()[name],high);
    f.input(id,'');assert.equal(f.nodes[id].value,normal);assert.equal(f.nodes[output].textContent,text);
    f.input(id,'invalid');assert.equal(f.prefs()[name],normal);
  }
  f.input('pace-factor',1.27);assert.equal(f.prefs().paceFactor,1.25);
  f.input('rpm',6742);assert.equal(f.prefs().rpm,6700);
});

test('combined power and grip stress does not compound through 5000 adjustments and exact restores',()=>{
 const f=performanceFixture(),physics=0xe18000,wheels=[0xe19000,0xe1a000,0xe1b000,0xe1c000];f.put(f.car+0x34,physics);
 wheels.forEach((w,i)=>{f.put(physics+0x38+i*4,w);f.d.setFloat32(w+0x188,1,true);});
 const base=f.read(0x230);
 for(let i=0;i<5000;i++){
  const s=f.e.state(),power=1+(i%21)/10,grip=1+(i%11)/10;
  f.e.tunePerformance(s,power,i%2===0);f.e.tuneGrip(s,grip);
  assert.equal(f.read(0x230),Math.fround(base*power));assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),Math.fround(.5*power));assert.equal(f.read(0x2c0),i%2===0?0:150);
  wheels.forEach(w=>assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(w+0x188,true),Math.fround(grip)));
  if(i%7===0){f.e.restorePerformance(s);f.e.restoreGrip(s);assert.equal(f.read(0x230),base);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),.5);wheels.forEach(w=>assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(w+0x188,true),1));}
 }
 f.e.restorePerformance(f.e.state());f.e.restoreGrip(f.e.state());assert.equal(f.read(0x230),base);assert.equal(f.read(0x2c0),150);
});

function interleaveBeforeCompare(e,action){const real=e.compareFloat.bind(e);let ran=false;e.compareFloat=(...args)=>{if(!ran){ran=true;action();}return real(...args);};return ()=>ran;}
test('apply and restore refuse a retired grip/ride identity immediately before a field operation',()=>{
 for(const type of ['power','grip'])for(const restoring of [false,true]){
  const f=type==='power'?performanceFixture():gripFixture(),s=f.e.state();
  const apply=()=>type==='power'?f.e.tunePerformance(s,1.5,true):f.e.tuneGrip(s,1.3);
  const restore=()=>type==='power'?f.e.restorePerformance(s):f.e.restoreGrip(s);
  if(restoring)apply();
  const retired=type==='power'?[...Array.from({length:9},(_,i)=>f.pi+0x230+i*4),f.pi+0x2dc,f.pi+0x2c0]:f.wheels.map(w=>w+0x188);
  const ran=interleaveBeforeCompare(f.e,()=>{f.put(f.car+(type==='power'?0x10:0x34),0xe80000);retired.forEach(p=>f.d.setFloat32(p,99,true));});
  restoring?restore():apply();assert(ran(),'interleaving was executed');retired.forEach(p=>assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(p,true),99));
 }
});
test('compare-and-swap preserves another writer after the final ownership check',()=>{
 for(const restoring of [false,true]){
  const f=gripFixture(),s=f.e.state();if(restoring)f.e.tuneGrip(s,1.3);
  const real=f.e.compareFloat.bind(f.e);let ran=false;
  f.e.compareFloat=(p,expected,value,guard)=>real(p,expected,value,()=>{const result=guard();if(!ran){ran=true;f.d.setFloat32(p,.8,true);}return result;});
  restoring?f.e.restoreGrip(s):f.e.tuneGrip(s,1.3);assert(ran);assert.equal(f.read()[0],Math.fround(.8));assert.deepEqual(f.read().slice(1),[1,1,1]);
 }
});
test('partial adjustment rolls back only successful owned fields when another field changes',()=>{
 const f=performanceFixture(),s=f.e.state(),real=f.e.compareFloat.bind(f.e);let count=0,ran=false;
 f.e.compareFloat=(p,expected,value,guard)=>{if(++count===4){ran=true;f.d.setFloat32(p,.77,true);}return real(p,expected,value,guard);};
 assert.equal(f.e.tunePerformance(s,2,true).changed,true);assert(ran);assert.equal(f.read(0x230),Math.fround(.2));assert.equal(f.read(0x23c),Math.fround(.77));assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),.5);assert.equal(f.e.performancePatch,null);
});

 }

test('unchanged power and grip factors avoid repeat atomic stores',()=>{
 const f=performanceFixture(),g=gripFixture(),s=f.e.state(),t=g.e.state();f.e.tunePerformance(s,2,true);g.e.tuneGrip(t,1.5);
 const original=Atomics.compareExchange;let count=0;Atomics.compareExchange=(...args)=>{count++;return original(...args);};
 try{for(let i=0;i<50;i++){f.e.tunePerformance(s,2,true);g.e.tuneGrip(t,1.5);}}finally{Atomics.compareExchange=original;}
 assert.equal(count,0);
});

function saveToolProfile(f,name='My driving',consent=false){f.input('profile-name',name);f.change('profile-network',consent);f.click('profile-save');return profileRecord(f).profiles.at(-1);}
function chooseToolProfile(f,profile){f.change('profile-select',profile.id);}
const fullProfileCaps={legacy:true,ai:true,pace:true,corner:true,walls:true,cars:true,dyno:true,dragAI:true,onlineTraffic:true,onlinePlayers:true,nativeDragOverheat:true};

 chooseToolProfile(restarted,p);restarted.click('profile-load');

 for(const id of ['online','traffic','players'])assert.equal(restarted.nodes[id].checked,false,id);

});

test('browser profile write locks serialize concurrent saves without dropping either profile',async()=>{

 const a=await pageFixture(null,false,false,{profileStorage:shared,profileLocks:locks}),b=await pageFixture(null,false,false,{profileStorage:shared,profileLocks:locks});
 a.change('nos',true);a.input('profile-name','Tab A');a.click('profile-save');b.input('profile-name','Tab B');b.click('profile-save');
 assert.equal(queue.length,2);assert.equal(queue[0].name,queue[1].name);assert.equal(a.nodes['profile-save'].disabled,true);assert.equal(a.nodes['profile-select'].disabled,true);assert.equal(a.nodes['profile-network'].disabled,true);
 // Even synthetic mutations while disabled cannot change the captured action.

 assert.deepEqual(profileRecord(a).profiles.map(p=>p.name),['Tab A','Tab B']);assert.equal(profileRecord(a).profiles[0].settings.nos,true);

});

# Changelog

## 0.42.8 draft — synthetic near-miss requests and confirmation handling

Adds a manual synthetic near-miss control with exact module/session ownership, one outstanding request, signed observed deltas, event-specific confirmation and cancellation without automatic retries. Automatic NOS refill stays disabled. Source and native integration checks are separate from installation and live verification; historical flag receipts remain pinned to their original experiments.

The synthetic award has no speed threshold. Native command ownership is deferred until initialized driving state; switching cars withdraws an unclaimed request, and restarting a session cannot reuse the previous bridge. Native CPU and guest stack state are preserved around the original award call.

Fixes the offline attribution counterexample: a different consumed event cannot be acknowledged as the requested synthetic event. Recovery abandons an obsolete witness so a subsequent distinct request is usable. Lost native ownership produces an unverified outcome and closes that witness. Whole-tick NOS changes remain visible and are not attributed entirely to one near miss.

## 0.42.7 — automatic NOS refill disabled pending integration

Disables the extension's automatic NOS refill at the page and direct Engine API while near-miss integration is tested offline. The control remains unavailable even with saved selections, restored profiles or online permission. Normal game-earned NOS and native NOS use remain available. No production near-miss award generation is enabled.

## 0.42.6 — direct worker loading and scoped 60946132 support

Adds the exact reviewed game build **60946132**. Its scoped native port covers the existing AI bridge, pace/corner hooks, rails, Drag handoff/protection, owned skill and paired catch-up. Online still requires the separate explicit permission. Stop, manual takeover, stale ownership and permission withdrawal retain their native guards.

The production page now supplies a verified compiled module through its existing game-worker startup observer. It leaves WebAssembly.compileStreaming unchanged. Per-worker message order, immediate port transfers, original shared-memory identity and primary/secondary worker consistency are checked offline. A timed-out, unsupported or failed preparation retains the original game module with tools disabled. Memory-port startup stays unverified and has no page memory tools.

The replacement is authorized by freshly read build metadata, an import/export interface check and complete source/output hashes. An opaque original compiled module cannot be hashed through this interface; matching its import/export names is an eligibility check, not proof of its bytes. Only the independently compiled replacement receives a verified tool profile.

On 60946132, **the tuner, leased forward geometry, per-target corner feedback, online car-category controls, race capture and destination travel are unavailable** pending their separate ports. Their implementations and previous build profiles remain included. The full 102c8d92 pipeline retains its exact prior output.

Current game guards, monitoring and report serialization are retained. A positive encoder result means serialization succeeded, including for reports containing observations. The offline checks do not establish multiplayer acceptance, account status or measured driving results.

The offline report check reproduced a selected-car-state observation from the actual NOS refill: one changed frame and observation flag 16 in controlled race and free-roam monitor contexts. Untouched baselines had zero changed frames and zero flags. The observed fields survived local encoding; no report was sent. This uses bounded native fixtures and synthetic session state, not a full game run. A different loader does not establish a report-free refill route.

The exact captured page check returned zero marks through updated startup and four fixture ticks; the frozen 0.42.5 startup produced API-wrapper mark 2. The fixture uses native-callable browser stand-ins, clean settings and default tool selections. Worker instance postMessage remains wrapped and is not selected by that captured check. Report markers and configuration remain unchanged. These page results do not cancel the separate native NOS observation.

Raw 60946132 SHA256: 81d2e32d7ee67bb93a8fafee4dbc17570f8d4980be238d7434e15c791904b945.
Scoped native output SHA256: 8efc4457e895e4992f56a0272f66718d3900901ff7fde95e760b7585fa6f9129.

## 0.42.5 — exact native corner-target feedback

Adds observed native target decisions to the road-race settings and diagnostics on verified game build **102c8d92**. A sample records the actual target before and after the existing corner-limit hook, requested/effective limit, decision outcome, guard reasons, ownership and sample age. These are **uncalibrated native target units**, not mph or m/s.

- The menu can distinguish a geometry reduction, cached reduction, an already-lower native target, a rejected/unresolved guard and a changed publication. This observes the existing driver; it does not change pace, braking, steering, grip, shortcuts or race outcomes.
- Receipts use the game's existing worker registration channel under the site's current security policy. The extension consumes its reserved messages before the game registry sees them. Current primary and secondary workers are bound to their module, memory and session.
- Stop/manual takeover, setting changes, ownership/permission loss, stale samples and route changes clear current evidence. Tick and command-sequence boundaries reject queued records from a previous activation. Existing historical race logs migrate without losing their prior columns.
- The optional observer must match its complete expected binary hash and compile before it receives a capability. Any failure keeps the previously compiled driving, online, tuner and forward-lease module.

Native parity, receiver, loader, page and diagnostic tests passed offline. The actual current worker also delivered a native receipt in isolated Chrome under its current CSP. This is not a live race or a measured driving improvement. Transport samples at most once per 1,000 guest ticks; it is not a lossless record of every setter call.

**Other work remains isolated:** the opponent Drag margin for tracks 4211–4213 passed controlled native tests but needs a proven production control connection; the default-off Drift bend-target experiment sometimes lowers native throttle or increases handbrake and needs a live comparison; destination routing passed controlled topology/GPS checks but has unresolved native queue/allocation, route-installation and parking issues. None of those experiments is activated by this package. A complete hosted travel → join → race → return loop remains unverified.

Saved profiles, stream HUD, radar, Clean View, tuner, Street X limits, Drag engine protection, explicit online permission and Stop/manual takeover keep their existing implementations. The preset tuner remains restricted to solo Performance Tuning; this release does not enable an ECU bypass.

Raw game SHA256: `2ba0b075721d80e75fc3fb9a3b0e4d2acae835d21fcc406d009669b83f81858d`.
Observed native output SHA256: `6005ed0fe49b641542e9e2909cf38d10108959f2d2ed2ac74144866281ad8cfc`.

## 0.42.4 — clear rails and catch-up controls

This update fixes misleading assistance controls. It does not change the native driving, cornering, grip, power, shortcuts, tuning or network policy from 0.42.3.

- In a permitted rails road race or Street X, the assistance row says **Race pace · rails mode**. Catch-up strength is visibly inactive because paired grip/power assistance is not used there. Its selected value is retained for full physics and Drag.
- Switching rails off restores the strength control. Drag keeps its strength control and neutral paired pace. Recovery continues to show speed-only behavior, including when a stale physics sample still says rails is on.
- Messages, tooltips and accessible labels now distinguish pace targets from paired handling assistance. Online permission, Stop/manual takeover and saved driving preferences retain their existing behavior.

Validation: controlled page/mode regressions cover solo and online road races, Street X, Drag, recovery, permission changes, Stop and preserved settings. No live lap or measured grip/speed improvement is claimed. The existing nativeRoadTarget diagnostic is a sampled value in uncalibrated native units; it is not a per-setter explanation. A new per-setter receipt remains research and is not included.

The route-geometry and cache-lease changes from 0.42.3 remain unchanged. They still require the appropriate active AI, rails and Adaptive road-race speed settings for Circuit/Sprint/URL; live driving verification remains pending.

## 0.42.3 — route-based corner limits and rails diagnostics

Supports the verified game build **102c8d92**. This update targets intermittent road-race corner control while retaining the existing tuner, Runway 15 loop, saved profiles, streaming displays, Stop/manual takeover and online permission.

- **Corner limits:** enable **Adaptive road-race speed** with **Stay on rails** and an active owned AI driver for Circuit, Sprint and URL. Online also requires **Allow network tools**. The current-build route sampler now supplies a corner-speed limit even when native corner records are empty. Controlled tests cover sharp and gradual bends, including 75-degree and sharper turns; straight targets and lower native targets are preserved. The existing selected pace still applies. Adaptive remains session-only and starts off.
- **Sample renewal:** a validated corner limit can remain usable while the next route sample is captured. The native driver retains and rechecks its original route, ownership, permission and age constraints. Slow or missing sampling does not extend the limit's lifetime. Stop and context loss revoke the request. The new sampler does not operate in Drag, Drift, Street X, free roam, recovery or full physics.
- **Rails recovery:** pause, focus loss and stopped game frames no longer advance recovery timers. Losing the HUD or permission does not reset the same race's two-release allowance. This fixes a reproduced recovery defect; it does not explain every reported wall hit.
- **Diagnostics:** brief rails transitions are retained within existing log budgets. Corner plans survive the shorter sampling callbacks long enough to be logged. The export distinguishes a requested limit, a native cache acknowledgement, renewal and expiry; an acknowledgement is not a claim of continuous application or collision-free driving.

The optional native lease stage is enabled only after its exact output compiles. If it is absent or fails, the previously compiled driving and tuner module remains usable with this new geometry feature disabled. Current raw game hash: `2ba0b075721d80e75fc3fb9a3b0e4d2acae835d21fcc406d009669b83f81858d`. Lease-adapted output: `842f84cdac800f39a292b0d82c3182f4e225a3e1663541473bdc76f10528aae2`.

Validation is offline: controlled actual-native sampling and speed-setter execution, route and permission guards, page scheduling, loader fallbacks and mode-preservation checks. No live driven lap or complete hosted travel → JOIN → race → return has verified this release. These changes do not establish perfect cornering, improved race results or streaming autonomy. The tuner remains solo Performance Tuning only; the ECU clamp-bypass recipe is still unavailable on this build.

## 0.42.2 — race loop, preset tuner and mode corrections

Supports the verified game build **102c8d92**. Circuit, Sprint and Drag retain their existing driving requests and native paths. Saved profiles, streaming HUD layouts, Stop/manual takeover and explicit online permission are preserved.

- **Race loop:** adds the missing current-build hosted-lobby and race-start mappings. **Runway 15 only** selects the unique normal Runway 15 start, sets Wait here and disables general Drag discovery so the loop stays on that race. It waits for an open host and repeats after the game returns; an absent or ambiguous start is reported. Press Start selected loop after selecting it. In career free roam, enable Allow network tools, choose race locations or open Drag-lobby discovery, and press Start. The loop uses the existing travel, stationary wait, exact JOIN, race and return flow. A missing, stale, full, private or changed host cannot become a create-lobby request. Offline state-machine and native JOIN dispatch checks pass; a complete live trip still needs verification.
- **Street X:** the 1.15× rails ceiling now also applies when a saved Custom race pace is selected. With rails off and paired handling selected, both driver and handling request neutral 1.00× pace so their guards agree. The menu distinguishes the applied request from the saved selection. Street X rails/recovery parks conflicting legacy power/grip. Other race types retain their selected pace.
- **Drift:** parks saved legacy power/limiter overrides while the native Drift driver owns or releases the car. Native Drift steering, scoring and full-physics behavior are unchanged. This removes a conditional interference source; it is not a verified higher-score driving algorithm.
- **Free roam:** current-build contact preview now recognizes cars eligible for the enabled no-clip categories, instead of unnecessarily reducing pace for them. Native corner assist remains eligible during bounded city pace reductions for the same owned car and route. Walls and unproven contacts still count. Free roam retains full physics; this does not put the city driver on rails or establish perfect cornering.
- **Preset tuner:** restores Load settings, all 41 editable fields, private native Preview/search, Stage selected preset and Restore for the current build. Capture can initialize the native policy cache, avoiding a disabled-Load deadlock. Both verified memory windows retain bounds and committed-page checks; invalid snapshots still fail S42. The tuner requires the **solo Performance Tuning main screen**. Online tune writes and the separate ECU clamp-bypass recipe remain unavailable.

For tuning: enable the preset tuner, select the race preset in the game's solo Performance Tuning screen, Load settings, edit or Find tune, review Preview, then Stage selected preset. Use the game's Test Run to refresh driving physics and Save Profile to persist. Estimates are private native calculations, not measured lap times or confirmation of a disk save. Restore requires the same unchanged car, parts and preset.

The combined loader grants tuner capabilities only after both its native bridge and private evaluator compile. A failed optional tuner/city stage retains the last successfully compiled driving module. Current game metadata was rechecked before packaging. Unknown builds remain unsupported until independently verified.

Validation is offline: actual native snippets, private evaluator, controller/state-machine tests, actual-manifest compile/fallback tests and an isolated Chromium panel smoke check. No live race, live tuning session or complete hosted travel → JOIN → race → return was driven for this release. Three older UI/trace assertions also fail on the frozen 0.42.1 baseline; five additional historical tuner tests cannot run because their archived research fixture is absent. These limits are recorded in the workspace handoff rather than presented as passing.

## 0.42.0 — game build 102c8d92, and "Stay on rails" for cleaner corners

- New game build: nfsu2.xyz now serves build 102c8d92. 0.41.0 did not recognise it, so the native AI driver would not load. 0.42.0 adds an exact profile for it (module SHA-256 2ba0b075…, 38,867,137 bytes).
- How the port was made: the reviewed ed8d3359 hook set (bridge, pace, corner and braking targets, walls and car contacts, Drag, Drift, nitrous, forward preview, route choice, catch-up, paired pace, skill 9) was replayed onto the new build as one pinned transform, `native-transplant-102c.js`. Every changed function keeps all of the new build's own instructions in order; only authored instructions are inserted, with function, type and host-address references moved to the new build's values. Input and output are pinned by SHA-256 (output f113eb5d…, 39,052,721 bytes) and the result must pass WebAssembly validation, or nothing is changed.
- Rails: the game drives opponents on a simplified physics mode and flips a car to full physics after a contact. Your racer record made that flip permanent for your AI-driven car, which is where the wall hits at raised pace came from. **Stay on rails** (Race / outrun tuning, on by default) keeps your race AI car on the simplified mode in solo Circuit, Sprint, URL and Street X. It is a guard in Car::SetPhysicsMode that only acts for the car the extension's AI owns, in a solo road race, while the page asks for it.
- On rails, Race pace + catch-up raises speed targets only (Paired race pace slider, default 1.30×; Street X at most 1.15× unless Custom race pace is on). The paired power/grip boost is not used on rails because it is far too strong on simplified physics. Drag keeps the paired boost. Turning rails off restores the 0.41.0 behaviour.
- Stuck watchdog: if the car stays under 2 m/s for 3 seconds the rails release so normal physics can recover it, and return after 2 seconds above 20 m/s. At most two releases per race.
- Solo/offline only on this build: Allow network tools is disabled, and online no-clip, city pacing and the hosted race loop are unavailable. The site's own online free-roam check (three host cells, re-read from the new build) still pauses every tool.
- Not ported to this build: the preset tuner / dyno / ECU panel.
- Unchanged for older builds: every earlier exact build keeps its own files and behaviour (the ed8d3359 chain still produces 41470ae5…).
- Offline checks: the shipped transform reproduces the tested module byte for byte and rejects a wrong hash, changed bytes, the old build and an already patched module; the rails guard passed 75 fixture cases on the real lifted function; the loader and the page-side controllers ran in Node on both builds, and the panel script ran in headless Chromium against a local stand-in for the site whose worker models the bridge (it is not the game). Nothing was driven live. The 1.30× default comes from older logs of one track.

## 0.41.0 — best-opponent skill 9 for your AI car, panel fixes

- Skill: your racer keeps the game's player marker (254, read as −2) in its skill field, and the game's AI code clamps that marker to skill 0, the weakest level. The AI driver's GetSkill() (0x402580, the only caller of the skill getter) now answers 9 for that marker at the seven call sites that clamp it: nitrous delay and decisions (0x40844b, 0x40d863, 0x40d91e, 0x416faa), the Drag launch reaction delay (0x42c105), a per-skill decision chance (0x4082e6) and a manoeuvre parameter (0x42d666). The racer record and the save are not written.
- It applies only while the extension's native AI owns the local player's current car (mailbox magic, even and stable sequence, heartbeat under 180, mode 1–2, active code, in world, one local player, car on an AI driver that is the car's current driver), and never in a network session, with or without Allow network tools.
- Left exactly as the game has them: the off-screen reset check (0x402263), target-speed variance (0x41c648, 0x41c9c9; the marker already gets none, any skill 0–9 gets some), the catch-up curve and update (0x4085e6, 0x417382, 0x417591), the branch choice (0x413e3c, owned by the shortcut policy) and four sites that discard the result.
- The Driver line says "skill 9 for nitrous and race decisions" (Drag: "skill 9 for launch and nitrous decisions") while it applies. There is no switch; it follows the AI driver.
- Fixed: the panel, the popup and exported logs still showed version 0.38.18 after 0.39.0 and 0.40.0. They now show the installed version.
- Fixed: with the game's Catch Up off, the Race pace + catch-up line said "Game Catch Up is off · matching boost unavailable" although the 0.39.0 boost was working. That line now appears only on builds without the player-only catch-up patch. Drag and Street X report their own waiting/applied state, and online sessions say "Off in online sessions · solo races only".
- Correction to the 0.40.0 note below: the game's global mode at 0x8650B0 makes normal skills read as 9 and keeps the player marker. It was never a way to give the player's car skill 9.
- Offline checks: 353 fixture cases on the real lifted wrapper (each site, each guard, online, other skills; everything except the returned skill is identical to 0.40.0), one real consumer (0x408430) through the game's own virtual dispatch, and the full patch chain, whose output 41470ae5… validates and compiles. Exact ed8d3359 only. Live racing is unverified.

## 0.39.0 — player-only constant catch-up

- Race pace + catch-up now works with the game's Catch Up flag off and Mods: Rubberbanding set to Off or No boost. Before, its native publisher required Catch Up on and Rubberbanding = Original, so with those off your AI car never got any catch-up. New `godly-catchup.js` (exact ed8d3359 only, applied after the paced catch-up patch, pinned input/output hashes) makes those two checks pass in the 7 gated native functions (36 sites each, same-length edits). Opponents keep whatever the game setting gives them.
- With Rubberbanding off the game's own factor is 1, so your car gets a constant pace × strength handling/power factor for the whole race, whether it leads or trails. It never "waits" like game AI does when ahead.
- New defaults: paired race pace 1.00× (corner targets at the game's own speed, fewer wall hits) and catch-up strength 1.50× (a bit above the game's own skill-9 maximum of about +37–42%). Raise strength for more push; raising pace raises corner entry speed.
- Catch-up assistance is never enabled in online/LAN sessions, even with Allow network tools on.
- Drag, Drift and Street X are still excluded from paired catch-up. The JS readGain helper no longer checks the Catch Up flag or the (wrongly mapped on ed8) Rubberbanding host.
- Offline checks: the full extension patch chain reproduces the shipped 0.38.18 module exactly (92b567a3…), the new output (e40e7798…) validates and compiles. Live racing is unverified.

# Optional native race geometry recorder

The integrated extension includes an optional native route recorder. The recorder has not collected a complete real race route or been tested in a live race. It does not enable AI, steer, brake or change tuning. Other driving features have their own verification limits in README and CHANGELOG.

## What it records

The recorder reads the owned driver's native race-planning window at the point where the game finishes its corner pass. It does not use free-roam GPS, the drawn map, screenshots, unrestricted asset downloads or opponent routes.

- Off by default, session-only, separate from all driving settings.
- Exact game build 93af6ccb only. Unknown builds do not activate it.
- Offline single-player ordinary race AI only. Online/LAN, drag, drift, special-mode flags, free roam and unsupported ownership are excluded, regardless of the existing online toggle.
- At most 256 windows, no faster than 10 requests/second, at most 40 nodes and 5 corner records per window. The recorder does not enable AI itself.
- No new native calls, steering, throttle, brake, target-speed, tuning, race-state or opponent writes. New writes are confined to its local 2 KiB request/response mailbox.
- Stops on observed identity/state changes, hidden/inactive tab, Stop, manual-control handback, game exit or timeout. An unsettled request or occupied mailbox requires a reload instead of automatic retries.
- Export is a local JSON download. Nothing is uploaded or stored in a tool profile.

## First bounded offline check

1. Update the contents of the existing stable `NFSU2-Driving-Tools` folder, reload its browser extension card, and refresh the game. Keep only that extension copy enabled. The recorder is available only on its exact verified game build.
2. Start an offline ordinary road race. Use the existing AI setting only if you want it to drive. Keep your existing working controls unchanged; capture does not require stronger pace, power, NOS or braking settings.
3. Open Session & diagnostics → Race geometry research → Record native route samples. Keep the tab focused. Stop after a short run, then choose Export route samples. Export before reload/closing; re-arming starts a new recording.

If the recorder reports zero sampled corner records, unknown data, a timeout or an unsupported state, report that result rather than assuming the road is straight. Export the partial recording if available. Do not repeatedly re-arm an unsettled request. Stop testing if the game behaves unexpectedly, and restore the working v0.33 extension.

## Meaning of the 75-degree analysis

The threshold is change of forward heading: 0° straight, 90° right-angle, 180° reversal. The analyzer combines same-direction turns within an ordered native record, so several gentler changes can reach 75°. Opposite-direction bends remain separate. Curvature below 75° is retained because a shallower bend may still need slowing at high speed.

Fresh side-sample markers, finite XY/distances and strictly increasing native distances are required before a record is treated as ordered. Duplicate points, missing pages, stale native tails, non-finite values, invalid ordering and excessive spacing remain unknown. An apparently straight map or straight chord is never proof that the underlying road is straight.

This analyzes sampled horizontal chords. It does not yet assemble windows into a complete race, verify the underlying spline between samples, detect all gentle bends spanning multiple windows, or measure altitude/banking. The native center is reused as the game's center; it is not claimed newly regenerated every pass.

## Identity and coverage

Career records include a verified event hash and native heat ordinal when the native pointer/count, event tuple, track, reverse and laps agree. Region is copied from a bounded TrackInfo field, and TrackInfo's track must agree. Quick-race career event/heat is explicitly unknown. Observed clock resets and career start-counter changes stop recording, but no universal attempt counter or perfect restart detection is claimed.

Each window remains partial. Repeated records are not unique-corner counts. Export always says `wholeRaceChecked:false` and `uniqueCornersVerified:false`. Actual complete race routes captured or verified so far: zero. This is not an “all corners protected” release and does not establish safer braking, faster laps or fewer collisions.

## Fresh offline recorder checks

- 24 native-observer, controller, geometry, loader and preservation tests pass in the current integration. Page control and complete extension regression results are reported separately by the release workflow.
- The complete exact-build modified module validates and compiles. Compared with the current verified AI patch, only the intended recorder route-updater function differs, and all its original instructions are retained.
- The authored observer rebuilds locally from the included builder and pinned evidence. Original game binaries and raw captures are excluded from the package.

Synthetic tests and compilation do not replace live validation. The next useful input is a short offline JSON capture, followed by route-order, coverage and braking-horizon validation. No automatic slowing based on this recorder has been enabled.

# NFSU2 Driving Tools: experimental v0.42.8 draft

## 0.42.8 — manual synthetic near-miss control

Adds a separate **Synthetic near miss → Award once** control. It publishes one request only after a verified native award service is connected to the current game module, memory and session. Unsupported builds and failed preparation leave the control unavailable. It is outside saved profiles and never runs automatically.

The synthetic award has no speed threshold. It uses the game's original style-award routine on the current owned car. Mailbox ownership starts after driving initialization; car changes cancel an unclaimed request, and a restarted session receives a new bridge.

Automatic NOS refill remains disabled. Synthetic near-miss awards also change style points and combo multipliers. The result distinguishes the native style award from the whole tick's observed style/NOS changes; those NOS changes are not isolated event-specific credit. Unknown, stale or mismatched acknowledgements cannot confirm the requested award, and a timed-out request does not retry. Stop, focus loss and withdrawn network permission request cancellation; only a matching native completion establishes the outcome.

This is a working source update. Packaging, installation and live gameplay verification have not been performed. Historical offline results below apply to their original source pins; motion generated by this extension has not yet been cleared by a complete native trajectory test.

## 0.42.7 — automatic NOS refill disabled pending integration

Automatic NOS refill is unavailable while the near-miss integration is developed and tested offline. The refill control stays disabled, and legacy preferences, restored profiles and online permission cannot activate it. The direct `Engine.refill` entry point returns false without changing memory. Normal game-earned NOS and the game's own NOS use remain available.

The bounded near-miss replay showed native credit with flag 0 under controlled phase order, but it did not validate a production extension connection or all client reports. Artificial awards also change style points and multipliers. No near-miss refill is enabled in this release.

The existing native transforms and source/output module pins remain those of 0.42.6. The historical checks below refer to their named versions and fixtures; they do not establish the loaded browser version, multiplayer acceptance or a new upstream game build. Reload the existing extension card and refresh the game after updating the loaded folder.

Per-worker message order, immediate port transfers, original shared-memory identity and primary/secondary worker consistency are checked offline. ## 0.42.1 — online native AI and car contacts

This update builds on the installed 0.42.0 package for exact game build 102c8d92. Network permission starts off unless deliberately restored by a consent-bearing saved profile. F7 takes control; F9 stops tools and clears permission.

- Circuit, Sprint, URL and Street X can use Stay on rails online for the locally owned AI car. The existing 1.30× paired race pace and 1.15× Street X ceiling remain (Custom race pace still overrides Street X). Rails raises speed targets only; Catch-up strength does not supply grip on rails.
- Drag keeps its distinct opponent-driver/shift path and engine protection. Its paired handling boost uses neutral paired pace. Street X with rails off also uses neutral paired pace. Native catch-up inputs, generation/identity guards and explicit network permission still control application; no constant grip or winning claim is made.
- Skill-9 decisions work for the owned AI car online at the same seven reviewed decision sites. The player's saved skill marker is unchanged. The display is current eligibility, not a count of those decisions firing.
- Online car no-clip can select traffic, other players and NPC rivals, including verified current race and Outrun participants. The local contact filter, bounded rosters and per-category switches are retained. It does not change walls or props, and a local skipped contact does not prove a remote client skipped it.
- Current-build online free roam is recognized using the verified host tuple. Missing tuple memory makes this build unready instead of treating it as solo. Free roam keeps its existing native driver; the race rails pin is not enabled there.
- Recovery now counts rails releases across a driver rebuild, while resetting for an actual race/player/context change. It retains the existing two-release maximum. Diagnostics export rails request/current state, pin count, recovery state, online adapter/permission eligibility and skill-9 eligibility, with migration of prior logs.
- Online capabilities are granted only after the exact native online module compiles. Missing, wrong, throwing or invalid adapters retain the verified 0.42.0 solo module. Unsupported forward readers remain disabled rather than being advertised by the native transplant alone.

Offline native, controller, actual-manifest and page checks are recorded in the workspace handoff. These do not establish live online race results, server acceptance, cornering on every track or streaming autonomy. The broad older UI suite retains two pre-existing stale text/style assertions, reproduced on unchanged 0.42.0; behavioral checks pass.

The tuner/dyno/ECU panel, hosted travel/join loop and forward road reader are still unavailable on this exact game build. This update does not port those features. Saved profiles and HUD layouts are not rewritten.

## Previous update — new game build and "Stay on rails" (0.42.0)

nfsu2.xyz moved to game build **102c8d92**. 0.42.0 supports it: the whole reviewed native hook set from the previous build is applied to the new one as a single pinned transform (`native-transplant-102c.js`), and the page-side addresses for this build are in `102c-profile.js` and the build registry.

**Stay on rails** (Race / outrun tuning, on by default) is the cornering fix. The game drives opponents on a simplified physics mode and switches a car to full physics after a contact. For your AI-driven car that switch was permanent, and on full physics a raised pace overshoots corners. On rails your race AI car keeps the opponents' mode in solo Circuit, Sprint, URL and Street X.

- On rails, **Race pace + catch-up** only raises speed targets. The **Paired race pace** slider is the multiplier (default **1.30×**; Street X at most 1.15× unless Custom race pace is on). No power or grip boost is applied and Catch-up strength is not used. Drag keeps the paired boost.
- If the car stops for 3 seconds, the rails release so the game's normal physics can recover it, then return once it is moving again (two releases per race at most).
- Turn Stay on rails off to get the 0.41.0 behaviour back.
- This build is **solo/offline only**: Allow network tools is disabled and the online tools are unavailable. The preset tuner / dyno / ECU panel is not ported to this build.
- Offline checks only; nothing was driven live. The Driver line shows "on rails" while the car is on the simplified mode.

## Best-opponent skill for your AI car (0.41.0)

When the native AI drives your car, the game still reads the player's skill marker (254), and its AI code clamps that marker to skill 0, the weakest level. From 0.41.0 the AI's nitrous decisions, Drag launch delay and per-skill decision chances use **skill 9**, the best opponent level, while the extension's native AI owns your car in a solo session. Your racer record and save are not written. Opponents and online sessions are untouched. Where the game already treats the player's car better than any opponent (no random target-speed variance, no off-screen reset), it is left alone.

The Driver line shows "skill 9 …" while it applies. There is no switch: it follows the AI driver. Exact ed8d3359 only. Live racing is unverified. This release also makes the panel show the installed version (it stayed on 0.38.18) and removes a wrong "Game Catch Up is off · matching boost unavailable" line.

## Player-only constant catch-up (0.39.0)

**Race pace + catch-up** now gives your AI car a catch-up boost even when the game's Catch Up option is off and Mods: Rubberbanding is Off. Only your car is boosted; opponents keep the game setting. The boost is constant to the finish line (pace × strength), not gap-based, so it never eases off while leading.

Defaults: paired race pace **1.00×**, catch-up strength **1.50×**. Turn on Race-only automatic driver, open AI driver → Road-race settings, and make sure Race pace + catch-up is on. 0.40.0 adds Drag and Street X (catch-up strength only, pace neutral). Drift is not covered. Never applied online. Exact ed8d3359 only. Live racing is unverified.

## Retained full-physics publication correction

An active automatic driver could stay waiting for handling-input publication because the full-physics hook checked the runtime CPU structure against guest-object bounds. The runtime CPU lives outside that guest region. The v0.38.10 correction gives the CPU its own aligned, full-state check against actual Wasm memory size, while retaining the strict bounds and commitment checks for the car, physics objects and guest stack. The native physics calculation, selected pace and strength formulas remain unchanged.

The focused native regressions exercise the full publisher with a high runtime CPU address and no guest commitment bit for that CPU. Matching handling inputs remain required before extra paired pace is confirmed. A later live v0.38.10 export on 943ee537 recorded full four-tire and simplified combined-input publication with applied handling receipts. That verifies those observed publication paths; it does not establish improved cornering, race wins or complete .11 behavior. Stop, manual takeover, saved profiles, Street X, Drag protection, HUD and the existing controls retain their behavior.

## Handling evidence and selected city pace

Race pace + catch-up pairs a selected extra race pace P (1–2×) with an independent catch-up strength S (1–10×, quarter steps). Strength changes the assistance, not the speed target. The initial selections are pace2× and strength1×; these are authored controls, not a claim about the game's maximum. Loading follows an already selected Automatic/Race-only driver and does not acquire a manual car.

On exact AA/15e/943 builds, paired assistance follows the native physics path already selected by the game. Full physics uses four tire inputs; ordinary simplified AI physics uses its combined-grip input. This update corrects receiver identities and supports those paths separately without forcing a different physics mode. The native driver/car catch-up source caches remain unchanged. From original publication M, the handling scalar/aerodynamic divisor E is f32(f32(M×P)×S), and the nominal grip input is f32(E×P). Native modifiers remain in the combined-grip path. These are handling inputs, not measured engine power, tire grip, speed gains or a guarantee of winning.

Extra pace waits for current matching physical-input evidence. Full and simplified physics use different evidence kinds; requested pace, requested strength and verified application remain separate. The tools panel says requested pace while physical support is waiting. Bounded acknowledgement-rejection and native-stage codes enter the local log to distinguish failed identity/output checks from an unobserved publication. Owner, command, actual physical output, mode or permission changes revoke gain. Raised corner targets retain native use-time checks. When paired support is unavailable, the corner fallback uses the same neutral pace as the final target, avoiding an extra division by the selected pace. The base grade and braking tables remain planning assumptions, not load/contact measurements.

Online city clearance pacing keeps your explicitly selected free-roam factor as its ceiling, including values above 1×. Clear or unavailable observations retain that selection; an observed wall/vehicle hazard can reduce the runtime request and recovery moves back toward your ceiling. Unchanged observations no longer compound the same reduction on every page tick. A timing interruption preserves the current same-owner slowdown and selected ceiling without adding recovery credit. Selected corner-planning pace stays stable while the separate city request changes, so the reduction does not rebuild the native driver. Existing exact-build online detection, current ownership, mode and permission checks remain. These partial observations do not establish route safety or collision avoidance.

Free-roam corner assist now compensates its approach-braking input by pace squared on these same three builds, matching its existing corner-speed compensation. Previously the braking hook skipped ordinary free roam while its target still received the selected extra pace. Actual native getter/approach fixtures at 1/1.5/2/3× prove the corrected approach envelope retains the native braking assumption. Lower/equal pace, race commands and special modes retain their existing paths. Ownership, route, table, mode, permission and use-time checks remain. This fixes a calculation mismatch; it does not prove that it caused an individual crash or change steering, traffic avoidance or recovery.

The streaming HUD and race hub use factual English track names, including Outer Ring, Bayview Plaza and Airport Circuit Track 5, for all 100 primary race IDs. The city is labelled Bayview. Unknown locations display as unavailable instead of internal track numbers. These names are a static factual projection of the user's existing game language table; no game language asset is packaged, and no new live memory reader is needed. Widget positions, sizing and Clean View keep their existing behavior.

The viewer HUD shows MPH, gear, RPM, location, places driven, top speed and driving time. MPH follows the native HUD's float32 conversion and truncation; it is the game's display convention. The session meter starts with this page and includes both manual and automatic free-roam/race driving. It credits only consecutive live samples no more than 500 ms apart, so hidden tabs, menus and invalid observations cannot add an unobserved gap. Saved race-history totals never become session records. Rear radar keeps its nearest distance and dot labels in game-distance coordinates without claiming independent metre calibration. Technical driving status remains in the tools panel.

Rotate camera is a separate toggle, off on reload. It requires Camera bound to C and uses that key at a random interval from 45 to 120 seconds during active driving. Menus, text entry, photo/drone mode, unfocused/hidden pages and changed sessions rearm a fresh interval. Pressing C postpones the next change; F7/F9 switch rotation off and release any automatic key pulse while preserving a real held C key. A current worker error also disables it. The toggle changes no performance settings and requires no online driving-tool permission. Timer and page-input fixtures are distinct from live camera verification.

Stop, manual takeover and profile Load disable paired assistance. Saved profiles retain their schema and custom values. Independent power/grip controls are parked while paired assistance owns an ordinary road race or awaits restoration. Street X, Drag, Drift, Outrun and free roam retain their separate controls. A matching verified handling path, game Catch Up On / Original and explicit online permission are required. Unattended streaming autonomy remains unfinished.

On exact game builds aa2429fb, 15e5958f and 943ee537, selected pace now scales the native speed factor when the racing AI consumes it. It leaves the native driver cache and vehicle catch-up factor untouched. The previous wrapper could multiply its own cached result again before the game's next refresh; actual native fixtures reproduced 1.95 → 3.80 → 7.41. This correction removes that authored cache mutation. Native corner/behavior limits and the optional forward target can still lower the resulting target. Street X uses its existing native tables and corner controls; it receives the cache correction without the ordinary-road shortcut policy.

Adaptive road-race speed also enables a targeted experimental shortcut-choice policy on aa2429fb, 15e5958f and 943ee537. The car's raw player skill marker254/signed−2 stays intact. Only the eligible owned Race action's branch-choice check consumes skill9 instead. Native graph, category, probability, direction, event and checkpoint rules stay in control. It does not force every shortcut, replace pathfinding, or prove that a real shortcut completes correctly. Drag, Drift and Street X remain excluded from that branch policy. Stop prevents further authored branch-choice substitutions; an already cached native decision can persist until the game replaces it.

The 250 ms local driving trace retains separate requested/applied pace, current native driver and car catch-up factors, target/control values, corner-record coverage and planner evidence. The new factor readings are bounded read-only observations. Shortcut installed/requested flags are not branch-use receipts. Previous v0.38.5 trace rows survive a same-tab upgrade with nulls for the new fields. Samples, offline native tests and compiled output checks are distinct from live-game verification.

The preceding v0.38.7 native-calculated mode requested extra pace1 and observed original publication at Off/100. The later paired controls keep pace and strength separate. The traced Original catch-up calculation has no fixed numeric upper clamp; neither pace2× nor strength10× is a native game maximum. Driver/car source caches stay native.
